title: Amortized Analysis Check
description: Relate rare expensive growth to amortized cost per operation.

questions.prompt: Across `n` pushes into a doubling dynamic array from empty, amortized cost per push is:
questions.explanation: Total over `n` pushes is still `O(n)`, so amortized per push is `O(1)`, even though rare resizes cost `O(current size)`.

options.text: Average cost per operation over a sequence; spikes can still happen

questions.explanation: Amortized `O(1)` ≠ every call is `O(1)` — spikes still exist. The average is over a sequence of operations.

questions.prompt: How does amortized analysis differ from average-case over inputs?

options.text: Amortized averages over a sequence of operations, not an input distribution

questions.explanation: Don’t confuse amortized with average-case over input distributions; here the “average” is over a sequence of operations.

questions.prompt: When capacity is full, a doubling growth `push` may:

options.text: Cost `O(n)` for that single call due to allocating and copying
Be free forever after the first resize

questions.explanation: That single `push` can cost `O(n)` when it allocates a larger buffer and copies old elements, but it happens rarely.
